newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hugo Boss sees 1997 sales up over 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hugo Boss sees 1997 sales up over 10 pct.

text.p: German fashion group Hugo Boss AG said on Friday it expected to post a sales rise of at least 10 percent this year although the pace of growth would slow in the second half.
The company reported a 17 percent rise in sales to 529.7 million marks ($288.8 million) for the six months ended June 30.
"The Hugo Boss board sees a double-digit sales rise in the 1997 business year as fully realistic," Boss said in a statement.
Some 11 percent of the first-half sales growth came from internal development while two percent was linked with favourable currency market developments.
Four percent of growth was linked with deliveries in advance of winter goods, which would help brake growth in the second half, Boss said.

After-tax profit rose 25 percent to 38.5 million marks in the period on the back of the higher sales although costs related to activities such as the launch of a golf-wear line and setting up new storage units in America and Germany weighed on earnings.
